1535-56672026Oct22Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear MedicineJ Nucl MedClinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.jnumed.126.27323210.2967/jnumed.126.273232Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.© 2026 by the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging.BentestuenMortenMDepartment of Nuclear Medicine and Clinical Cancer Research Center, Aalborg University Hospital, Aalborg, Denmark; This patient had untreated gastric cancer at the time of AA diagnosis, and surgery was difficult because of thrombocytopenia. CsA and ROMI as a bridging therapy to curative surgery may therefore represent a feasible treatment option in patients with AA complicated by malignant tumors. 1476-55942026Oct21OncogeneOncogeneFatty acid 2-hydroxylation restrains gastric cancer by blocking CD36 palmitoylation and fatty acid uptake.10.1038/s41388-026-04021-2Fatty acid (FA)-induced internalization of the FA transporter CD36 normally functions as an intrinsic brake on FA uptake and lipid overload, but cancer cells can bypass this checkpoint to sustain lipid-fueled growth. The mechanism underlying this failure remains unclear. Here, we identify a FA 2-hydroxylase (FA2H)-CD36 signaling axis that operates as an endogenous brake on lipid fueling in gastric cancer cells. FA2H-derived (R)-2-hydroxy palmitic acid ((R)-2-OHPA) disrupts CD36 interaction with its palmitoyltransferase DHHC4, thereby limiting CD36 palmitoylation and trafficking to the plasma membrane. Loss of FA2H permits CD36 palmitoylation and establishes a feed-forward loop that amplifies FA uptake, lipid accumulation, and tumor growth. Restoring FA2H expression or supplementing cells with exogenous (R)-2-OHPA reinstates the lipid-sensing checkpoint. Moreover, FA2H activation sensitizes gastric cancer cells to inhibition of endogenous FA synthesis through blockade of FA synthase (FASN) or stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD1). In vivo, (R)-2-OHPA treatment or expression of the palmitoylation-deficient CD36 AASS mutant attenuates FA2H deficiency-driven lipid accumulation and tumor growth, positioning CD36 palmitoylation as the critical effector in this metabolic circuit. Together, these findings establish FA 2-hydroxylation as a metabolic checkpoint that links FA structure to CD36 trafficking and FA utilization in gastric cancer, revealing a targetable vulnerability in lipid-driven tumor growth.© 2026. In this study, we demonstrate that the basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) shows increased DNA-binding activity and expression in GC tissues and cell lines, based on assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analyses. Additionally, in GC cells, BATF forms droplet-like nuclear condensates. Using combined approaches of chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq, we find that BATF condensation promotes its binding to the TM4SF1 promoter and enhancer regions, thereby regulating TM4SF1 transcription and prompting the TM4SF1-driven formation of focal adhesions and GC metastasis. 1437-77722026Oct21International journal of clinical oncologyInt J Clin OncolRe-evaluating the neutropenia-survival paradigm in irinotecan-based therapy for advanced gastric cancer: post-hoc analysis of the RINDBeRG trial.10.1007/s10147-026-03221-wChemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN) has been considered a favorable prognostic marker across multiple cytotoxic regimens for gastrointestinal malignancies. However, its prognostic relevance in irinotecan (IRI)-based therapy for advanced gastric cancer (AGC) remains unclear.This post-hoc analysis used data from the phase III RINDBeRG trial comparing ramucirumab (RAM) plus IRI with IRI monotherapy as third- or later-line treatment for RAM-refractory AGC. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated according to the occurrence of grade 3 or higher neutropenia, defined as CIN. OS was also evaluated according to the baseline absolute neutrophil count (ANC), stratified by quartile-based cutoffs.Among the 393 patients in the safety population, 44.5% and 28.5% in the RAM + IRI and IRI arms developed CIN, respectively. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, with some imbalances across baseline ANC groups. In the RAM + IRI arm, those with and without CIN had a median OS of 9.7 and 8.9 months, respectively (HR = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.13; p = 0.25). In the IRI arm, those with and without CIN had a median OS of 8.4 and 8.6 months, respectively (HR = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.60-1.19; p = 0.34). Higher baseline ANC was associated with shorter OS, particularly in the RAM + IRI arm (7.3 vs. 10.9 months; HR = 1.83; 95% CI 1.14-2.94; p = 0.01).Unlike other cytotoxic regimens, CIN was not associated with survival in AGC patients receiving IRI with or without RAM. The clinical relevance of baseline ANC warrants further investigation.jRCT2031200106.© 2026. 1437-77722026Oct21International journal of clinical oncologyInt J Clin OncolElectronic patient-reported outcome monitoring and quality of life during later-line nivolumab therapy for advanced gastric cancer.10.1007/s10147-026-03213-wHealth-related quality of life (HRQoL) often deteriorates during later-line treatment for advanced gastric cancer. Although nivolumab monotherapy has been an established treatment option in this setting, HRQoL data remain limited. This study aimed to examine associations between symptomatic adverse events (AEs) and HRQoL deterioration and to evaluate the feasibility of home-based electronic patient-reported outcome (ePRO) monitoring.This prospective observational study enrolled patients aged ≥ 20 years with an ECOG performance status of 0-2 who were scheduled to receive later-line nivolumab monotherapy in clinical practice. Patients self-reported symptomatic AEs using PRO-CTCAE and assessed HRQoL weekly using FACT-Ga via a smartphone-based ePRO system for 12 weeks. The association between symptom deterioration and HRQoL decline was analyzed using a general linear model. Digital literacy and impressions of ePRO were also surveyed.Among 29 evaluable patients, 20 completed the 12-week monitoring period. Median time to HRQoL deterioration was 9 weeks. Several symptomatic AEs, including stomatitis, dysgeusia, pain, malaise, and depression, showed nominal associations with HRQoL decline in unadjusted exploratory analyses (all nominal p < 0.05). Despite 37.9% of patients not regularly using smartphones, adherence to ePRO reporting was high, with only 0.95% missing data.Exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between specific symptomatic AEs and HRQoL deterioration during later-line nivolumab therapy for advanced gastric cancer. ePRO monitoring achieved high data completeness, although patient acceptability was limited. These findings support further evaluation of ePRO as a tool for timely symptom recognition, alongside strategies to improve acceptability.© 2026. 1437-77722026Oct20International journal of clinical oncologyInt J Clin OncolSafety and efficacy of neoadjuvant S-1 and oxaliplatin therapy for gastric cancer in the elderly: combined phase II trials of KSCC1601 and KSCC1801.10.1007/s10147-026-03204-xThe efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in elderly patients with locally advanced gastric cancer remains unclear. We evaluated neoadjuvant S-1 plus oxaliplatin (SOX) therapy in elderly patients using patient data from two phase II trials.Patient data from KSCC1601 and KSCC1801 phase II trials were integrated. Patients were divided into an elderly group (age ≥75 years) and a non-elderly group (age <75 years). Adverse events, postoperative complications, and outcomes were compared. Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were calculated from treatment initiation.Among the 73 patients enrolled in trials, 66 (90.4%) underwent surgery and 65 (89.0%) achieved R0 resection. Neoadjuvant SOX therapy was administered to 69 patients (94.5%). Among those with R0 resection, 22 were aged ≥75 years and 43 were aged <75 years. PS 1 was significantly more common in the elderly group, with no other baseline differences. Postoperative complications developed in 11 patients (16.9%), including 1 (4.5%) in the elderly group and 10 (23.3%) in the non-elderly group (p = 0.12). Grade III or higher complications occurred only in the non-elderly group. OS and RFS did not differ significantly between the age groups (OS: Hazard ratio (HR) = 0.78, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 0.27-2.21, p = 0.64; RFS: HR = 1.12, 95% CI 0.51-2.44, p = 0.79). Undifferentiated histology, stage III disease, and poor pathological response were associated with worse survival.Neoadjuvant SOX therapy is feasible in selected elderly patients with locally advanced gastric cancer and yields survival comparable to those of younger patients.© 2026. 2051-142614102026Oct20Journal for immunotherapy of cancerJ Immunother CancerNeutrophil-epithelial niches arrest B-cell maturation in dysfunctional tertiary lymphoid structures of gastric cancer neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy.e01630110.1136/jitc-2026-016301Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are widely viewed as favorable in cancer immunotherapy, yet their clinical impact varies dramatically, and the local determinants of TLS quality remain poorly defined.We integrated spatial transcriptomics, matched single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex tissue imaging, in vitro perturbation assays, orthogonal spatial-proteomic validation, and external bulk transcriptomic cohorts encompassing more than 1100 patients to define TLS functional states and their associated immune-ecological determinants in gastric cancer.We identify a single fate-determining TLS subtype in which response-divergent germinal-center and plasma-cell trajectories unfold. In non-responders, B cells arrest at a naive/antigen-presenting state through collapse of a mid-trajectory NF-κB licensing module. This arrest is imposed by a coupled peri-TLS niche of FCN1_neutrophils and an ATF4-driven, immunologically silent tumor-epithelial state. Incidence during 2000-2023 was analyzed using Joinpoint regression. A clinical cohort diagnosed during 2004-2023 at prespecified stomach subsites (C16.1-C16.6, C16.8, and C16.9) was compared across four periods. Surgery trends were decomposed into stage-composition and within-stage components. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), cause-specific survival (CSS), and 36-month restricted mean survival time (RMST); adjusted Cox models separately summarized associations over 0-60 months.The clinical cohort comprised 66,391 tumor records from 66,025 patients. Incidence declined during 2000-2019 (annual percent change, -1.32%; 95% CI, -1.61% to -1.08%) and increased during 2019-2023 (4.96%; 95% CI, 2.51-9.91%). Comparing 2004-2008 with 2019-2023, distant-stage disease increased from 36.1% to 43.0%, whereas surgery among records with known surgery status decreased from 51.9% to 36.3%. Stage-composition change represented 25.7% of the surgery decline. Recorded chemotherapy increased from 35.7% to 54.4%. Median potential follow-up was 206.0 versus 27.4 months; latest-period fixed-time estimates were reported at 12 and 36 months. Three-year OS increased from 25.2% to 29.1% and CSS from 31.4% to 35.6%. Unadjusted 36-month RMST differences were 1.80 months (95% CI, 1.47-2.15) for OS and 1.86 months (95% CI, 1.53-2.22) for CSS.Distant-stage presentation became more frequent while recorded surgery declined and short-term survival improved modestly. Within-stage changes represented most of the surgery decline. Additional registry years are needed to assess persistence of the post-2019 incidence increase.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. 2688-15352026Oct20JCO oncology practiceJCO Oncol PractSelection and Management of Patients With Resectable Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer Receiving Perioperative FLOT: A Modified Delphi Consensus Approach.OP2600462OP260046210.1200/OP-26-00462Perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is a guideline-recommended standard for patients with resectable gastric cancer or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma globally. Guidance is limited on patient selection, nutritional optimization, and toxicity management within existing guidelines. This study aimed to develop an international consensus to address these management gaps.A modified Delphi methodology, informed by the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, was conducted virtually between March and August 2025. A multidisciplinary panel of 16 experts independently rated draft clinical statements across multiple domains. Responses were anonymized, with structured, iterative rounds of feedback and re-rating. Consensus was defined a priori as a median score of 7-9 (appropriate) or 1-3 (inappropriate) with a disagreement index ≤1.0.Consensus was reached on 66.3% of the statements. Experts agreed that patients aged >70 years should not be routinely excluded from perioperative FLOT but require comprehensive assessment; inclusion of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) 0-1 is appropriate, and ECOG PS 0-2 may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Adequate organ function, correction of baseline conditions, hepatitis B screening, and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase testing are appropriate before FLOT initiation. Universal baseline nutritional screening and support, proactive intervention for malnourished patients, and structured physical activity were endorsed. Surgical planning was supported through multidisciplinary input, with defined perioperative windows, individualized dosing, and flexibility in pre-/postoperative cycles. For toxicity management, the panel supported dose modification over drug omission, where possible.This Delphi consensus provides expert-driven, practice-oriented advisories codifying fitness-based selection, nutrition-forward optimization, and pragmatic toxicity management. 1941-66365712026Oct20Journal of gastrointestinal cancerJ Gastrointest CancerNeoadjuvant Therapy for Gastric Adenocarcinoma with Signet Ring Cells: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.24010.1007/s12029-026-01620-wSignet ring cell-containing gastric cancer constitutes an increasingly recognized subtype. Although perioperative chemotherapy is the standard of treatment for locally advanced gastric cancer, its efficacy in signet ring cell-containing gastric adenocarcinomas remains controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess the impact of neoadjuvant chemotherapy compared to upfront surgery on overall survival.A systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane was conducted up to January 2026. Eligible studies included adult patients with signet ring cell-containing gastric cancer undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery compared to upfront gastrectomy. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool hazard ratios for overall survival.Six studies, including seven cohorts and 5.388 patients, were included. The pooled analysis demonstrated no significant difference in overall survival between neoadjuvant chemotherapy and upfront surgery (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.68-1.34, I2 = 83.2%). Subgroup analyses by studies' geographic origin and design revealed consistent results with no significant differences in overall survival among Western (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.53-1.38, I² = 86.9%) or Eastern studies (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.63-1.97, I² = 83%), and among different study designs (randomized controlled trial: HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.81-1.67; observational: HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.62-1.38, I² = 85.5%).Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was not associated with a significant improvement in overall survival compared with upfront surgery in signet-ring cell-containing gastric cancer. While perioperative chemotherapy remains the recommended therapeutic approach, further studies employing contemporary chemotherapy regimens are warranted to define its role in this distinct histological subtype.© 2026. B, BiointerfacesColloids Surf B BiointerfacesInternalizing RGD (iRGD)-modified liposomal nanoparticles as a universal antigen-delivering platform for remodeling tumors and enhancing T-cell receptor-engineered T cell immunotherapy.11626611626610.1016/j.colsurfb.2026.116266S0927-7765(26)00854-4T cell receptor-engineered T cell (TCR-T) therapy holds promise for solid tumors but faces challenges from insufficient and non-uniform antigen presentation and inefficient T-cell tumor delivery. Current strategies that rely on endogenous tumor antigen expression are often limited by transcriptional silencing or downregulation of target antigens in a substantial fraction of tumor cells, resulting in incomplete tumor recognition. To address this, we developed iRGD-modified liposomal nanoparticles (iRNY-LNPs) as a universal antigen-delivering platform for remodeling tumors and enhancing TCR-T immunotherapy. The iRNY-LNPs, co-assembled from DSPE-PEG-iRGD and DSPE-PEG-NY-ESO-1 (New York Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma-1), exhibited a uniform size of 206.3 ± 5.4 nm and demonstrated significantly enhanced penetration into 3D tumor spheroids compared to non-targeted nanoparticles. In vitro, iRNY-LNPs enabled uniform NY-ESO-1 antigen presentation on tumor cells, potently activating TCR-T cells and enhancing interferon-γ secretion and cytotoxicity. In vivo imaging confirmed efficient tumor accumulation and retention of iRNY-LNPs. In a gastric cancer model, the combination of iRNY-LNPs and NY-ESO-1 TCR-T cells achieved 73.0% tumor growth inhibition and significantly prolonged survival, with no observed systemic toxicity. This study establishes a proactive tumor-remodeling strategy that circumvents the reliance on endogenous antigen expression by enforcing uniform antigen display. Given its modular design based on lipid-peptide conjugates, the platform can be readily adapted to deliver other tumor-associated antigens by simply substituting the peptide moiety, offering a versatile framework for TCR-T immunotherapy against diverse solid tumors.Copyright © 2026. 1432-099183122026Oct19Current microbiologyCurr MicrobiolMolecular Detection Technologies for Helicobacter pylori Antibiotic Resistance: Current Status and Clinical Implications.59810.1007/s00284-026-05136-1Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infects approximately half of the global population and is closely linked to chronic gastritis, peptic ulcers, and gastric cancer. Antibiotic resistance has become a major global health concern with marked regional variations, severely undermining empirical treatment efficacy. Resistance mechanisms primarily involve target gene mutations, efflux pump overexpression, and altered membrane permeability. This review summarizes resistance mechanisms of commonly used antibiotics against H. pylori, along with diagnostic approaches ranging from phenotypic to molecular methods, the latter offering faster and more precise mutation detection, yet limited by high costs and invasive sampling. Treatment has shifted from clarithromycin-based triple therapy to bismuth-containing quadruple and potassium-competitive acid blocker-based regimens. However, susceptibility-guided therapy faces implementation barriers, and empirical regimens remain prevalent. Future directions emphasize affordable multiplex molecular platforms, resistance surveillance networks, artificial intelligence-driven predictive models, and non-antibiotic adjunctive strategies. Integrating molecular diagnostics with antimicrobial stewardship to transition from empirical to precision-based management is critical for improving eradication rates and curbing further resistance spread.© 2026.
